explain.say: Sensors on the wheels measure the real speed, and the computer compares it with the set speed. The difference tells it whether to add or reduce engine power.

explain.say: Going up a hill, gravity pulls back and the car slows slightly, so the controller opens the throttle to push harder until the forces balance again. Going down, it eases off.
Adaptive cruise control adds a radar or camera to watch the car ahead. If that car is slower, the system reduces speed to keep a safe gap, then speeds up again when the road clears.

faq.q: How does cruise control know the speed?
faq.a: It reads the wheel speed sensors, the same ones used by the anti-lock brakes, and turns their pulses into the car's speed.
asks: What sensor does cruise control use?

faq.q: How does cruise control go up hills?
faq.a: As the hill slows the car, the measured speed drops below the set speed. The controller opens the throttle for more power until the speed recovers.
asks: Why does the engine get louder on hills with cruise control?

faq.a: It adds a radar or camera that measures the distance and speed of the car ahead. The system slows down to keep a safe gap and speeds back up when the lane clears.
asks: How does adaptive cruise control work?

faq.q: How do you switch off cruise control?
faq.a: Pressing the brake or clutch, or the cancel button, switches it off at once, handing control back to the driver.
asks: How do I cancel cruise control?

faq.q: Is cruise control a closed-loop system?
faq.a: Yes. It constantly measures the actual speed, compares it with the target, and corrects the engine power, which is exactly what closed-loop feedback control means.

facts: Engineer Ralph Teetor invented modern cruise control; it first appeared on 1958 Chrysler cars.
Adaptive cruise control uses radar or cameras to keep a set gap to the car in front.

quiz.say: A car on cruise control starts climbing a hill. What does the system do?
quiz.why: The car starts to slow, so the controller opens the throttle to hold the set speed.

wrong.1: Hills do not switch it off; it corrects for them.
wrong.2: Braking would slow it further; it needs more power.
